faq.q: How is a titanium derailleur limit screw manufactured?
faq.a: A typical titanium derailleur limit screw is manufactured using CNC machining of tooth profile; Thread rolling; Swiss-type turning. BOZE CNC Ti uses precision CNC equipment with strict process controls to ensure consistent quality and dimensional accuracy.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V for titanium derailleur limit screw?
faq.a: Alternative materials include stainless steel (heavier, susceptible to corrosion) and aluminum (lower strength, shorter fatigue life). The alternative manufacturing method is Cut (machined) threads (reduces fatigue life by 200% due to interrupted grain flow).

faq.q: What standards apply to titanium derailleur limit screw?
faq.a: Titanium Derailleur Limit Screw components are typically manufactured to ASTM B348. Additional customer-specific specifications may apply.

faq.q: What are common failure modes for titanium derailleur limit screw?
faq.a: Common failure modes include Surface contamination from iron pickup during machining requiring acid passivation (ASTM F86). BOZE CNC Ti mitigates these through strict process control, proper material selection, and 100% inspection.
